title: Quick Accent is Unstable and contain Crashes.

judgment.rationale: The report describes repeated Quick Accent exits and severe lag in medium/heavy applications on Windows 10 but gives no exact PowerToys version, Windows build, triggering input sequence, or diagnostics. Those gaps prevent distinguishing a Quick Accent process failure from an unrelated application or system slowdown.
evidence: The reporter selected Microsoft Store installation and Quick Accent, described Windows 10 UEFI, repeated exits, and lag as low as 1 FPS.
The version field says only 'Stable Version'; expected behavior and bug-report ZIP are blank.
No follow-up comments, attachments, or concrete reproducing app/shortcut are present.
judgment.recommended_action: Request the exact PowerToys and Windows builds, a numbered Quick Accent input/affected-app sequence, and a fresh /bugreport immediately after the failure.

fix_assessment.rationale: There is no reproducible failure transition or diagnostic evidence to identify a PowerToys code fix; the Windows 10 UEFI mention alone cannot establish ownership.

issue_context.summary: Quick Accent reportedly exits repeatedly and coincides with severe lag in some applications on Windows 10; the exact trigger and installed versions are unknown.
known_information: The issue names Quick Accent, Microsoft Store installation, and Windows 10 UEFI.
The reporter describes repeated Quick Accent crashes, closing itself, and medium/heavy apps slowing to about 1 FPS.
The exact PowerToys version, Windows build, expected behavior, affected application, reproduction steps, and bug report are absent.
inferences: The reported lag might coincide with Quick Accent activation, but the report cannot yet establish that Quick Accent causes the application slowdown.
issue_context.analysis: A small reporter evidence package can first separate a reproducible activation/process exit from a system-wide performance problem. Ask only for versions, the failing input/app sequence, and diagnostics captured immediately after the failure.
initial_investigation: Read the complete live report and metadata; no comments, attachments, linked fixes, or specific crash evidence clarify the failure path.

information_gaps.why_needed: Distinguish Quick Accent activation failure from an unrelated app or system slowdown.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Write short numbered steps naming the foreground app, keys pressed, and what exits or slows first.

information_gaps.information: Fresh PowerToys diagnostics immediately after the failure

actions.label: Request Quick Accent repro and diagnostics

comment.body:
Thanks for reporting the repeated Quick Accent exits and the severe lag in larger apps on Windows 10. To tell whether Quick Accent is crashing during activation or whether another app is causing the slowdown, please provide:
1. The exact PowerToys version from Settings > General > About and the Windows 10 version/build from `winver` (the report currently says only 'Stable Version' and 'Windows 10 UEFI').
2. Short numbered steps: name the foreground app, the exact keys you press to invoke Quick Accent, what appears, what closes first, and whether the 1 FPS lag also occurs with Quick Accent disabled.
3. Immediately after reproducing the exit or lag, submit a comment containing `/bugreport` so the generated ZIP captures that occurrence. Please review it for sensitive information before sharing.
These details will identify a reproducible Quick Accent failure path and show whether the lag is related.

status.label: Quick Accent repro needed
status.detail: Windows 10 crashes and lag are reported, but the version, trigger, affected app, and diagnostics are missing.
